title: Biological Foundation Models — records under review
description: Audited candidates excluded from the displayed canonical index until their scope, artifact, identity, duplication, or reuse-term issue is resolved.

record.name: DeepSEA
record.description: Pioneering deep-learning sequence model that predicts 919 chromatin features (TF binding, DNase, histone marks) from DNA with single-nucleotide sensitivity to prioritize noncoding variants.
record.io: DNA sequence (~1 kb) -> 919 chromatin feature predictions; noncoding variant effect scores
record.status: HOLD: no written historical-exception policy; original 2015 release (standalone DeepSEA v0.94b, ~803 MB) is served again from deepsea.princeton.edu/help/ over HTTPS (reachability intermittent) with no licence stated; successor Sei is catalogued as bfm-sei
record.use_cases: Noncoding/eQTL/disease variant prioritization, chromatin feature prediction, regulatory sequence analysis
record.audit_note: replace the October host-unavailable sentence: on 2026-11-06 the HTTPS help page returned 200 and the standalone archive HEAD 200 (802,952,421 bytes, Last-Modified 2025-01-28); HTTP still 404. '919 features' and '1000 bp input' now verified against the official help page. No licence on the page. Trained network file inside the archive not seen.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06. Scope: still no written historical-exception or supervised multi-task predictor policy (MAINTENANCE.md unchanged since 2026-07-14). Artifact: improved — the original release page https://deepsea.princeton.edu/help/ is serving again (HTTP 200 over HTTPS; HTTP still 404; it was 503 in October, so reachability is intermittent) and offers the standalone DeepSEA v0.94b archive (HEAD 200, ~803 MB) with no licence or terms stated. The trained network file inside the archive was not seen (partial header read only). Sei remains displayed as bfm-sei. The policy decision is now the main blocker. Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; see evidence/refresh-2026-11-06/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider when (a) a written historical-exception or supervised multi-task predictor policy is adopted in MAINTENANCE.md; then re-confirm (b) that https://deepsea.princeton.edu/help/ and the standalone archive are still reachable, record terms as 'no licence stated (all rights reserved by default)', and confirm the trained-model file from an archive listing. If (a) is adopted but the host is unreachable again at that review, retire in favour of bfm-sei.

record.name: ChromBPNet
record.description: Kundaje-lab bias-factorized, base-resolution CNN of chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq/DNase-seq), trained for each dataset. A frozen pretrained enzyme-bias model is combined with a trainable TF sub-model to reveal motif syntax, TF footprints and regulatory variant effects.
record.io: DNA sequence -> base-resolution accessibility profiles; TF motif/footprint and variant-effect outputs
record.status: HOLD: MIT code; CC-BY-4.0 reference bias models on Zenodo; 1,512 per-dataset trained models (ENCODE DNase-seq/ATAC-seq, 5 folds each) public and ungated on the kundajelab Hugging Face organisation with MIT card licence (3 of 1,512 checked), also on ENCODE/Synapse (terms there not checked); no single broadly pretrained model
record.use_cases: cis-regulatory syntax discovery, TF footprinting, regulatory variant scoring, enhancer/accessibility modeling
record.audit_note: append: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06 — found the kundajelab HF 'ENCODE ChromBPNet Atlas' (1,512 ungated per-dataset repos, MIT card licence on 3 sampled); preprint still v4; MAINTENANCE.md unchanged. Blocker is the scope decision only.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06. Preprint still v4 (2026-09-23), not journal-published; no new release or default-branch commit. New: the official kundajelab HF org now hosts an 'ENCODE ChromBPNet Atlas' of 1,512 ungated per-dataset model repos (1,143 DNase-seq, 369 ATAC-seq; 408 biosamples; 5 folds each; card licence MIT, 3 sampled). This is a compendium of per-dataset checkpoints, not a single model pretrained for reuse across datasets, and MAINTENANCE.md (unchanged since 2026-07-14) has no policy admitting assay-specific predictors or model compendia. The blocker is now purely the scope decision; the reusable access route exists. Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; see evidence/refresh-2026-11-06/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider when MAINTENANCE.md gains a written scope policy that explicitly admits assay-specific sequence-to-function predictors or model compendia of per-dataset checkpoints (the HF ENCODE ChromBPNet Atlas would then satisfy the artifact side, subject to a full licence sweep beyond the 3 sampled repos), or when the developers release and document a single pretrained ChromBPNet-family model intended for reuse across datasets or cell contexts. This hold is a curator decision; no further external evidence is needed to decide it.

record.name: Mistral-DNA

record.io: DNA sequence -> embeddings, next-token likelihoods (zero-shot variant scores), generated DNA; fine-tuned classification heads
record.status: HOLD: public ungated checkpoints with apache-2.0 model cards; repository code has no licence; no primary paper or technical report; README still links a non-public v0.1 checkpoint
record.use_cases: Genomic sequence classification, DNA generation, fine-tuning for regulatory/variant tasks, teaching/tutorials
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06: unchanged. 15 public ungated Mistral-DNA-v1 checkpoints; 17M/138M/422M hg38 cards declare apache-2.0 with safetensors. review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; no change. Checkpoints and weight terms re-confirmed (15 public ungated v1 checkpoints; hg38 cards apache-2.0). Still missing: a developer-authored paper, preprint or technical report describing the released v1 checkpoints (Europe PMC, arXiv and one web search found none; two other Mourad papers from 2024 and 2026 do not mention Mistral-DNA). review.reconsider_when: Reconsider when a developer-authored primary description (paper, preprint or technical report/release note) of the released Mistral-DNA-v1 checkpoints (training corpus, objective, evaluation) is verified, or when the curator records in writing that developer-authored GTN tutorials plus model cards suffice as primary documentation (precedent: MarinDNA accepted an official release write-up). record.status: HOLD: task-specific localization classifier and conditioned generator; MIT code and CC BY 4.0 checkpoints exist, but broader foundation-model scope is not established

No broader foundation-model scope is documented and no written task-specific exception exists. The Science page returned 403; the abstract was read via Europe PMC. review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06: unchanged. record.status: HOLD — scope: single-task docking pose predictor. MIT code, a 464 MB checkpoint linked from the README (Dropbox) and a hosted Bohrium app exist, but MAINTENANCE.md has no written structural/docking exception.
record.use_cases: Binding-pose prediction, structure-based virtual screening, lead optimization
record.audit_note: Exact model is a dedicated docking predictor rather than an unambiguous broader-than-one-task FM. HOLD or document a structural/docking exception. Paper, repo.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; unchanged. MAINTENANCE.md still has no structural/docking exception (no matching text; last changed 2026-07-14). All primary sources still describe a single-task protein-ligand pose predictor (README, arXiv v1 only, ICANN 2025 chapter); docking code untouched since 2024-08-28. Reusable Uni-Mol encoders remain catalogued as bfm-uni-mol. Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; see evidence/refresh-2026-11-06/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if MAINTENANCE.md adopts a written structural/docking exception (applied consistently with displayed docking-adjacent records such as bfm-flowdock), or if an official release documents reuse beyond binding-pose prediction. record.name: ScDiVa
record.description: Masked discrete-diffusion single-cell foundation model (12-layer bidirectional transformer, about 94.5M parameters) that jointly models gene identity and continuous expression magnitude with a latent anchor token; pretrained on 59 million cells.
record.io: Masked/corrupted single-cell expression -> denoised gene identities + magnitudes, cell embeddings, generated cells
record.status: HOLD — Apache-2.0 code and ungated Apache-2.0 weights; the corrected GitHub loader matches the hub checkpoint, but the 41,818-gene vocabulary needed to tokenize new data is not released and the hub-hosted loader is outdated
record.use_cases: Single-cell generation, dropout/sparsity-aware denoising, joint identity-and-expression modeling, representation learning
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The September loader defect is fixed on GitHub: scdiva/modeling_scdiva.py reads model.safetensors with safetensors.load_file, pins config and weights to one hub revision and loads strictly with no random-init fallback; the safetensors header of the unchanged hub checkpoint (128 tensors, 94.5M parameters) matches every parameter name and shape in that code. Checked statically; nothing was downloaded or executed. Still missing: the 41,818-gene vocabulary or tokenizer needed to encode new data (absent from the GitHub tree, the hub model files and the hub dataset). The hub model card and hub-hosted modeling_scdiva.py still show the superseded loader that falls back to random weights. Unrelated scDIVA methods remain distinct (arXiv 2602.03477).

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06: unchanged since October. Code (GitHub, last push 2026-10-02) and weights (hub, unchanged since 2026-02-05) are Apache-2.0 and ungated, and the corrected GitHub loader matches the checkpoint. The 41,818-gene vocabulary or tokenizer needed to map new expression data to the checkpoint's gene IDs is still absent from the GitHub tree, the hub model files and the hub dataset, so the checkpoint cannot be applied to new cells. The hub card still shows the superseded loader example. Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; see evidence/refresh-2026-11-06/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Promote when an official source (GitHub or the hub repo) publishes the 41,818-gene vocabulary or tokenization code that maps new expression data to the checkpoint's gene IDs. Record then as Apache-2.0 code and weights, noting in the audit note if the hub model card still shows the superseded loader. Keep disambiguation from unrelated scDIVA methods (e.g. the bioRxiv tumor-immune scDIVA integration method).

record.name: scDrugPerturb-Bench
record.description: Mechanism-annotated benchmark linking matched control and drug-treated single-cell RNA-seq profiles to literature-curated key-gene response evidence, with a Mechanism Fidelity Score for evaluating drug-perturbation prediction models.

record.use_cases: Mechanism-aware evaluation and model selection for single-cell drug-perturbation predictors
record.audit_note: Re-checked 2026-11-06. Code is unlicensed. The data are a preview only, under 'other' with no rights granted, and full access is by contact. Preprint only. The bioRxiv paper link uses the DOI form and was checked through the bioRxiv API, not the doi.org resolver.

review.reason: Partly resolved. record.name: AmbiModBench
record.description: Evaluation benchmark for genetic-perturbation response prediction that pairs every score with a train-mean reference on the same split, screens readouts by gene-coordinate permutation and relates gains to embedding-space coverage, using Perturb-seq data from K562, RPE1 and Norman.
record.status: HOLD: MIT code (anonymized review mirror only; results tables CC BY 4.0); derived benchmark data on Hugging Face labelled MIT, ungated; no own model weights. Upstream Perturb-seq data keep their own terms.
record.io: Perturbation-model predictions on frozen splits (protein-embedding inputs) -> MSE/Pearson/top-gene recall paired with train-mean and reference-pool baselines, permutation screens
record.use_cases: Checking whether single-cell perturbation models learn target-specific responses beyond the shared background; leakage-aware zero-shot TF-perturbation splits
record.audit_note: Preprint v1 only (2026-09-26). Code exists only as an anonymized double-blind mirror; data on a personal Hugging Face account (MIT label). README scope (TF-perturbation, K562 490-TF cohort) narrower than the abstract. Upstream Replogle/Norman data terms not checked; archive not downloaded.

review.reason: October blocker (no code/data link) is partly resolved: the arXiv full text (v1 only, 2026-09-26) now points to an anonymized review mirror at anonymous.4open.science, whose file API lists an MIT LICENSE (results tables additionally CC-BY-4.0), src/, tests/ and a README linking benchmark data on Hugging Face (wozhen/ambimod: public, ungated, card licence mit, 13 files incl. split manifests and ESM2/ProTrek embedding tables). Remaining blocker: there is no permanent, attributable official repository (the code exists only as a double-blind anonymized mirror; the data sit on a personal HF account), and the README scope (zero-shot TF-perturbation benchmark, 490-TF K562 cohort, 15 frozen splits) is narrower than the paper abstract (K562, RPE1, Norman). Upstream Perturb-seq terms were not checked. GitHub repository search failed (HTTP 403 search rate limit), so a de-anonymized repo may exist unseen.
review.reconsider_when: A permanent, attributable official repository (de-anonymized) is published with the licence, and the released benchmark matches the paper's K562/RPE1/Norman scope.

record.name: RNADynBench
record.description: All-atom RNA molecular-dynamics benchmark of 2,585 quality-controlled 100-ns trajectories of 1,469 unique RNAs (GROMACS, Amber OL3, OPC water) with leakage-controlled structural and high-flexibility test splits for trajectory generation and dynamics-descriptor prediction.
record.status: HOLD: Trajectory data publicly downloadable from Box without login; no licence stated (licence 'Coming soon', so all rights reserved by default); evaluation code and RNADynNet weights not released.

record.audit_note: Preprint v1 only. Data released without a licence or DOI; evaluator, code and RNADynNet weights pending. Box contents seen as a folder listing only; trajectories not downloaded.

review.reason: Partly resolved since October: RNADynBench v1.0 data are now publicly downloadable from an Imperial College Box share (trajectories, metadata, protocol, splits, SHA256SUMS; stored snapshot RNADynBench-v0.1-20261001) and a 2,585-row trajectory catalog CSV is public. Without a licence the trajectories are all-rights-reserved by default; RNADynNet (the model) is not covered and has no released weights.
review.reconsider_when: A data licence and dataset DOI are published for RNADynBench, ideally with the evaluation code; RNADynNet would need released weights to be considered as a separate model record.

record.name: OpenBind (first release)
record.description: Open experimental structure-affinity dataset for the EV-A71 2A protease (CVA16 surrogate): 925 crystallographic binding events from 699 compounds with KD measurements for 601, plus prepared inputs and docking and cofolding benchmark outputs.
record.status: HOLD: Experimental data CC0; benchmark inputs and docking/cofolding outputs CC BY 4.0, except the AlphaFold3 run archive, which falls under the AlphaFold3 Output Terms (non-commercial organisations only). No own model weights.

review.reason: No change in the blockers. Zenodo search (sorted newest) still shows only the August 2026 EV-A71/CVA16 2A protease records: the CC0 experimental data release (22142262; 925 crystallographic binding events, 699 compounds, affinities for 601), the CC BY 4.0 benchmark-outputs record (20798528) whose files include zip_run_af3.zip, a GNINA outputs record, and the OpenBind-0 benchmarking materials. bioRxiv preprint still v1 (2026-09-01, CC BY); Europe PMC shows no second OpenBind release. The AF3 prediction archive falls under the AlphaFold3 Output Terms (non-commercial organisations only), as handled for SABLE. OpenBind-0 (model) is already an alias of bfm-openfold3; this lead is the dataset/benchmark. Single-target scope remains the deciding issue.

record.name: LongevityBench
record.description: Benchmark of 17 aging-biology tasks across epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, clinical and genetic data, rendered as chat prompts with deterministic scoring, used to compare frontier LLMs and fine-tuned Longevity-LLMs.
record.status: HOLD: Benchmark data CC BY-NC 4.0 on Hugging Face (not gated); source datasets keep their own terms; non-commercial terms apply.

review.reason: Artifact and terms are clear and unchanged: Cell article (Europe PMC, PMID 42753698, 2026-09-01) and the public, ungated Hugging Face dataset (CC BY-NC 4.0; benchmark, mini and extra configs; card updated 2026-10-06). The blocker is still scope: the benchmark scores LLMs on chat-formatted omics prompts (the card says it evaluates 'large language models on quantitative aging-biology tasks'), and the accompanying Longevity-LLMs are fine-tuned general LLMs. PG-LLM is a catalog precedent for an LLM-facing benchmark, but extending it to general omics-in-prompt benchmarks is a maintainer decision.
review.reconsider_when: Maintainer decides whether LLM benchmarks on text-rendered omics belong in the benchmark modality (precedent: PG-LLM).

record.name: DART-Eval
record.description: Benchmark of DNA language models on regulatory DNA with five tasks: prioritising known regulatory elements, transcription-factor motif footprinting, discriminating cell-type-specific elements, predicting chromatin activity from sequence, and chromatin-activity variant-effect prediction.
record.status: HOLD: Evaluation code on GitHub with no licence file (all rights reserved by default); task data on Synapse, downloadable after free Synapse login, no access requirements and no licence stated; no own model weights.
record.io: Regulatory DNA sequences + DNA language-model embeddings or likelihoods -> element prioritisation, motif sensitivity, cell-type activity and variant-effect metrics
record.use_cases: Choosing DNA language models for regulatory-genomics tasks; comparing them with supervised baselines on regulatory elements and variants
record.audit_note: No licence on code or data. Synapse download needs a login; access verified via the Synapse REST API (no access requirements). Task list taken from the Synapse wiki task headers; evaluation settings not re-read from the paper; data not downloaded.

Code half unresolved: GitHub API licence field null and licence endpoint 404 (last push 2026-03-22). Both code and data therefore carry no licence (all rights reserved by default). Identity confirmed by Crossref (NeurIPS 37, 2024; Patel ... Kundaje).
review.reconsider_when: A licence is added to the GitHub repository or the Synapse data, or the maintainer accepts no-licence benchmarks with precise status wording (precedent: ViroBench code).

record.name: scVision
record.description: Vision foundation model for single-cell transcriptomics from Stanford that renders each cell as an image by placing genes on a fixed, optimal-transport-derived pan-tissue layout, then pretrains a vision transformer by masked image modelling on 72 million human cells. The frozen encoder is used without fine-tuning for zero-shot cell-type annotation, gene-program recovery and multi-study integration.
record.status: HOLD: Web service only: hosted live model behind a free Google-sign-in account, with no documented inputs/outputs, API or terms of use; no code or weights released; project page marked all rights reserved.
record.io: Single-cell raw counts rendered as a gene-layout image -> frozen encoder cell embeddings for zero-shot annotation, gene-program recovery and integration
record.use_cases: Zero-shot cell-type annotation, unsupervised gene-program recovery, multi-study integration without batch labels
record.audit_note: Checked 2026-11-06. Preprint not peer reviewed (arXiv v1, 15 Jul 2026). No code or weights; the only access route is an account-gated hosted app whose functions and terms are undocumented on its public pages (not signed in). noncommercial=false reflects absence of stated terms, not a permissive licence; the project page says all rights reserved.

review.reason: New since October: the arXiv comment names a project page (islamlab.org/scvision), which links a hosted 'live scVision model' at app.islamlab.org/scvision behind a free Google-sign-in account. The project page links no code, weights or licence, and its footer reads 'All rights reserved'; the app page documents no inputs, outputs, API or terms of use. GitHub search found only the lab website repository; Hugging Face search found nothing. Substantive in-scope single-cell model (Stanford; 72M cells, frozen encoder for zero-shot annotation and integration) with a specific, checkable blocker: no released weights or code, and the only access route is an undocumented account-gated service with no stated terms. Service contents were not inspected beyond the public landing pages; no sign-in attempted.
review.reconsider_when: The authors release code and encoder weights (or document the hosted service's inputs, outputs, API and terms of use).

record.name: EventHorizon
record.description: Self-supervised foundation model for clinical flow cytometry from ARUP Laboratories and the University of Utah: a hierarchical, marker-aware transformer pretrained by self-distillation on 100,937 routine clinical specimens (over 50 billion cells) that integrates heterogeneous multi-tube panels into one specimen-level embedding.
record.status: HOLD: No public code or weights; weights and embeddings only on reasonable request for non-commercial research, subject to ARUP/University of Utah approval, IRB review and a data use agreement, with no guarantee of access. Pretraining data not public.
record.io: Multi-tube clinical flow-cytometry specimen (events x markers, variable panels) -> specimen-level embedding for lightweight downstream classifiers
record.use_cases: Diagnostic classification of hematologic malignancies, detection of recurrent AML genetic abnormalities from embeddings, cross-site lymphoma and AML transfer, B-ALL measurable residual disease detection
record.audit_note: Checked 2026-11-06. Preprint not peer reviewed (v2, 10 Oct 2026). No released artifact: access is by request only, non-commercial, conditional on institutional approvals and a DUA, and explicitly not guaranteed. Trained on single-institution clinical data.

review.reason: October blocker now answered: the v2 full-text HTML has a Data and Code Availability section. Weights and embeddings are shareable only on reasonable request, for non-commercial research, subject to ARUP and University of Utah administrative approval, IRB review and a data use agreement, and sharing 'cannot be guaranteed'. Pretraining data (ARUP clinical records) are not public. GitHub and Hugging Face name searches found no official artifact. Substantive in-scope model (cytometry is routed to singlecell, as for CytoBERT) with a specific, checkable blocker: no released weights and no guaranteed access route.
review.reconsider_when: Weights are deposited or a formal controlled-access procedure with stated terms is published by the authors.

record.name: GeneICL
record.description: Small (about 4.2M-parameter) tabular in-context foundation model for bulk gene expression from the Boeva lab (ETH Zurich), pretrained only on a semi-synthetic prior built from measured bulk expression profiles. Given a labelled support set of expression profiles it predicts query labels in context, without gradient updates, for classification, regression and Cox-style survival.
record.status: HOLD: Open code + weights: MIT repository and PyPI package; checkpoints (about 25 MB each) ship in the package (seed 0) and the repository (seeds 1-2); not gated; no API or server.
record.io: Labelled support set + query bulk expression profiles (samples x genes, log1p-CPM, any gene set) -> in-context class labels/probabilities, continuous values or Cox risk scores and survival functions
record.use_cases: Clinical outcome prediction from bulk transcriptomes (classification, regression, survival) with small labelled cohorts, without per-task training
record.audit_note: Checked 2026-11-06 (GitHub API, git tree, PyPI JSON, arXiv API). Preprint not peer reviewed. Scope/modality routing pending curator ruling (bulk-transcriptomic tabular in-context model; 'multimodal' proposed by analogy with OmicsFM). Pretraining prior is semi-synthetic, not direct self-supervision on biological data. Default checkpoints in 1.1.0 differ from the paper's v1.0.0 model (shipped as CKPT_V1). The repository's eval/ folder also carries third-party baseline weights (e.g. LimiX-16M, COMPASS) whose own terms were not checked; they are not part of GeneICL. Nothing downloaded or executed.

review.reason: Artifact and terms are now fully verified: MIT licence for the whole repository (GitHub licence API), releases v1.0.0 (2026-10-07) and v1.1.0 (2026-11-02), PyPI geneicl 1.1.0 (MIT) whose wheel ships the seed-0 checkpoints, and ~25.6 MB checkpoint files for the classification, regression and v1.0.0 (paper) families visible in the git tree. The remaining blocker is the curator scope ruling from October, which I did not make: the model is pretrained only on a semi-synthetic prior built from bulk expression profiles and does in-context classification, regression and survival on any bulk expression table. Precedent for routing: OmicsFM (bulk proteomics/transcriptomics profiles) was placed under 'multimodal' on 2026-10-10. If the curator accepts bulk-transcriptomic tabular models, the proposed record below can go straight to the catalog.
review.reconsider_when: The curator rules whether bulk-transcriptomic tabular in-context models are in scope and confirms the modality (proposed: multimodal, as for OmicsFM).

record.name: ProteinTalks
record.description: Neural ordinary differential equation virtual-cell model pretrained on more than 38 million time-resolved protein-abundance measurements from drug-perturbed breast cancer cell lines, then used for drug efficacy and synergy prediction, resistance-protein interpretation and transfer to organoids and clinical biopsies.
record.status: HOLD: MIT-licensed code and a single best checkpoint in the GitHub repository (licence file in the ProteinTalks subfolder only); training data on Google Drive; Nature article subscription-only.
record.io: Baseline proteomic profile + perturbation descriptor + drug fingerprints/physicochemical features -> predicted proteome at 6/24/48 h and drug efficacy or combination-synergy probability
record.use_cases: Drug efficacy and synergy prediction, drug-combination discovery, resistance-associated protein interpretation, patient/organoid response stratification
record.audit_note: Repository found by code search, not via the paper (Nature full text unreadable); licence only in subfolder; modality for perturbation-proteomics models not yet assigned by curator; released checkpoint is a breast-cancer drug-response model, so scope is borderline.

review.reason: Artifact blocker partly resolved: GitHub code search found the Guo lab (guomics-lab; last author Guo T) repository PTV-1 with a ProteinTalks/ folder holding training/prediction code, an MIT LICENCE.md (copyright 'yonggeli66') and a 10.1 MB best_checkpoint.pth committed 2026-09-04; training data linked on Google Drive. Remaining blockers: (1) the Nature article is still subscription-only and its code-availability statement could not be read, so the paper-to-repository link is unconfirmed (the 2025 bioRxiv preprint text I read cites only db.prottalks.com for data); (2) repo-level licence is undetected by GitHub (licence file sits in the subfolder only); (3) curator modality routing for a bulk perturbation-proteomics neural-ODE model is still open, and scope is borderline: the released checkpoint is the joint proteome-dynamics + drug efficacy/synergy model trained on breast-cancer cell lines. A 2025 bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.02.07.637070, v1 2025-02-10, v2 2025-02-12) is the first public version. A third-party 'lattiasg/ProteinTalks' demo repo (created 2026-10-22) was not treated as official.
review.reconsider_when: The Nature code-availability statement (or the repo README) confirms guomics-lab/PTV-1 as the official ProteinTalks release, and the curator assigns a modality and confirms scope for perturbation-proteomics virtual-cell models.

record.name: WILSON

record.use_cases: Patient-level pathology classification, slide/case retrieval, diagnostic report generation, treatment-response prediction
record.audit_note: Preprint only; no artifact released; release is conditional on publication and ethics clearance; terms unknown (pending patent noted).

No WILSON model found on Hugging Face. Substantive in-scope slide/case-level pathology model with a stated, checkable release trigger, so it suits the under-review register.

record.description: Tri-modal contrastive model from the Zhi Huang lab that aligns multiplexed immunofluorescence (CODEX) spatial-proteomics patches, matched H&E histology and clinical-metadata text in one embedding space, trained on 26.7 million mIF patches from 3,218 tissue sections of 1,606 patients across 11 organ types; Haiku(Bi) is a bi-modal H&E-mIF variant without the text encoder.

record.use_cases: Cross-modal retrieval between spatial proteomics, histology and clinical text; survival and clinical prediction; zero-shot biomarker inference from H&E; exploratory counterfactual analysis of tissue niches
record.audit_note: Preprint only; code has no licence; weights manually gated with unreadable terms; noncommercial=true inferred from the bundled MUSK component (CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0), not from Haiku's own terms.

Huang Z) is the primary preprint and its Code Availability names github.com/zhihuanglab/Haiku and huggingface.co/zhihuanglab/Haiku (the October lane missed it because the repo citation block is still a placeholder). Haiku_state_dict.pt present in both repos (3.2 GB / 2.8 GB per README).
review.reconsider_when: A licence file is added to the GitHub repository or the Haiku hub card states readable licence/gate terms.

review.reason: Unchanged since October: arXiv 2608.26208 (latest version updated 26 Sep 2026) and repo lugia-xiao/GITIII_scale (last push 31 Aug 2026) still have no licence (gh api license=null, no LICENSE file in root listing), and the two checkpoints (v0.pt, v1.pt) are still only on personal Google Drive links (view pages reachable, nothing downloaded). record.name: JEPA-DNA (NV-JEPA-DNA)
record.description: NVIDIA continual-pretraining framework that adds a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture latent-prediction objective (with VICReg-style regularisation) to the native MLM or next-token objective of existing genomic language models.
